beats.say: Find K, for P equals P nought E to the power K T.
Here is the plan: use the start to find P nought, then use the doubling, then take L N.
To start with means T equals zero. E to the power zero is one, so P equals P nought.
asks: Why is E to the power zero equal to 1?

beats.say: It starts at one hundred, so P nought is one hundred.
asks: What does to start with mean?

beats.say: Doubles every seven point five hours: at T equals seven point five, P is two times one hundred, two hundred.

do.on: at T equals seven point five

beats.say: Put them into the model. P is two hundred at T equals seven point five.
asks: Which values go into the model?

beats.say: And P nought is one hundred: two hundred equals one hundred E to the power seven point five K.
Divide both sides by one hundred. E to the power seven point five K equals two.
The E part is alone, and E is involved, so take L N of both sides.
asks: Why take L N and not log?

do.on: take L N of both sides

beats.say: Bring the power down: seven point five K comes down in front of L N E.
asks: Why can the power come down?

beats.say: L N E is one, because E to the power one is E. So seven point five K equals L N two.
asks: Why is L N E equal to 1?

beats.say: Divide by seven point five: K equals L N two over seven point five.
So K is zero point zero nine two four, correct to three significant figures.
asks: How do I key ln 2 over 7.5?

beats.say: Watch out: when it doubles, P is two hundred, not two. Doubling one hundred gives two hundred.
